name: Self-Updater
description: Keeps a server checkout in sync with its Git repository: deploys new commits or release tags, restarts PM2, Docker, Compose or systemd services, checks health and rolls back on failure. Polling or webhooks, no runtime dependencies.
sites_https_justification: Project sites use HTTPS only: GitHub, Cloudflare Pages (configuration builder), npmjs.com and ghcr.io.
description_good_justification: The README opens with what the software does: it keeps a server checkout in sync with its Git repository, deploys new commits or release tags, restarts the service, checks health and rolls back on failure. https://github.com/VectoDE/Self-Updater/blob/main/README.md
interact_justification: The README covers installation, configuration and the configuration builder and links the security policy and the contributing guide; SUPPORT.md points to issues and Discussions. https://github.com/VectoDE/Self-Updater/blob/main/README.md
contribution_justification: Contributions go through GitHub pull requests; the process is documented in https://github.com/VectoDE/Self-Updater/blob/main/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md
floss_license_osi_justification: Apache-2.0 is approved by the Open Source Initiative.
documentation_basics_justification: The README documents installation, quick start, every configuration option, the CLI commands, webhooks, notifications, running it with systemd, PM2 or Docker Compose, the container image and the migration from self-updater 1.x-3.x. The configuration builder at https://self-updater.pages.dev/ checks a configuration with the same validation code. https://github.com/VectoDE/Self-Updater/blob/main/README.md
documentation_interface_justification: The external interface (configuration file format, CLI commands and exit codes, webhook endpoint, library API and the /config entry) is documented in the README, and the exported functions and types carry TSDoc that ships in the .d.ts files. https://github.com/VectoDE/Self-Updater/blob/main/README.md
repo_public_justification: Public git repository on GitHub: https://github.com/VectoDE/Self-Updater
repo_track_justification: git tracks every change, its author and time.
repo_interim_justification: All interim changes are committed to the public repository and go through pull requests before release.
repo_distributed_justification: git is a distributed version control system.
version_unique_justification: Every release gets a unique SemVer version, from package.json and the git tag. https://github.com/VectoDE/Self-Updater/releases
version_semver_justification: The project uses Semantic Versioning, stated in the changelog; the release workflow picks major, minor or patch from the pull request labels.
version_tags_justification: Releases are tagged in git. From v4.0.0 on, the release workflow creates a signed annotated tag for every release. Older tags are v1.0.0, v1.0.1 and 1.0.2; self-updater 3.0.0 was published to npm without a tag. https://github.com/VectoDE/Self-Updater/tags
release_notes_justification: Human-readable release notes per version in https://github.com/VectoDE/Self-Updater/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md and on the GitHub releases (the release workflow uses the changelog section as the tag message and release notes).
release_notes_vulns_justification: No release so far fixed a publicly known vulnerability. The security policy requires fixed vulnerabilities to be listed under "Security" in the changelog, with the CVE where one applies. https://github.com/VectoDE/Self-Updater/blob/main/.github/SECURITY.md#what-happens-next
report_process_justification: Bug reports go to GitHub issues with issue forms: https://github.com/VectoDE/Self-Updater/issues
report_responses_justification: There were no bug reports from other people in the last 12 months; reports are acknowledged by the maintainer.
enhancement_responses_justification: There were no enhancement requests from other people in the last 12 months; requests are answered by the maintainer.
report_archive_justification: GitHub issues and pull requests form a public, searchable archive: https://github.com/VectoDE/Self-Updater/issues?q=is%3Aissue
vulnerability_report_process_justificati: The reporting process is published in https://github.com/VectoDE/Self-Updater/blob/main/.github/SECURITY.md#reporting-a-vulnerability
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: Private reports go through GitHub private vulnerability reporting (enabled): https://github.com/VectoDE/Self-Updater/security/advisories/new
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: The security policy promises a first answer within 7 days; there were no vulnerability reports in the last 6 months.
build_justification: npm run build (tsdown) builds ESM, CommonJS, types and the CLI into dist/; docker build builds the container image. Documented in https://github.com/VectoDE/Self-Updater/blob/main/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md#setup
build_common_tools_justification: Builds with npm, TypeScript and tsdown; the container image with Docker. These are common tools for this ecosystem.
build_floss_tools_justification: Node.js, npm, TypeScript, tsdown, Go and Docker (Moby/BuildKit) are all FLOSS.
test_justification: Automated test suite with Vitest: unit tests, integration tests that deploy, roll back, follow tags and check SSH signatures against real Git repositories created in the temp directory, and property-based tests with fast-check. Run with npm test, documented in https://github.com/VectoDE/Self-Updater/blob/main/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md#setup . Tests: https://github.com/VectoDE/Self-Updater/tree/main/test
test_invocation_justification: Tests run with the standard npm test command.
test_most_justification: Coverage is about 98 % of statements and 95 % of branches; vitest.config.ts enforces at least 95 % of lines, statements and functions and 90 % of branches.
test_policy_justification: Policy: new functionality and bug fixes come with tests, and a bug fix with a test that fails without it. https://github.com/VectoDE/Self-Updater/blob/main/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md#making-a-change
tests_are_added_justification: Recent changes added tests, for example the fix that keeps operator commands and health URL tokens out of logs (commit 99d486c) added tests in test/health.test.ts, test/schema.test.ts and test/updater.test.ts.
warnings_justification: TypeScript strict mode (with noUncheckedIndexedAccess and exactOptionalPropertyTypes) type-checked with TypeScript 6 and 7, ESLint with typescript-eslint strictTypeChecked and stylisticTypeChecked plus sonarjs, and Prettier run in CI.
warnings_fixed_justification: CI fails on any warning (eslint --max-warnings 0, tsc --noEmit); there are no open warnings.
know_secure_design_justification: The maintainer applies secure design: no runtime dependencies, Git and built-in restarts without a shell, tokens passed through the environment instead of URLs or arguments, webhook deliveries checked in constant time before parsing, least-privilege CI tokens, pinned actions and provenance-signed releases.
know_common_errors_justification: The maintainer knows the common errors for this kind of software (command and argument injection, secrets in logs and process arguments, webhook spoofing and timing attacks, resource exhaustion, race conditions between deployments) and documents how they are countered in https://github.com/VectoDE/Self-Updater/blob/main/docs/ASSURANCE.md#common-weaknesses-countered
crypto_published_justification: Only published algorithms are used: GitHub webhook signatures are checked with HMAC-SHA256 and compared in constant time. Commit and tag signatures are checked by Git (OpenSSH or GnuPG). No own cryptographic algorithms.
crypto_call_justification: HMAC-SHA256 and the constant-time comparison come from Node's built-in node:crypto (createHmac, timingSafeEqual); TLS from Node.js and Git; signature checks from git verify-commit / verify-tag. Nothing is reimplemented.
crypto_floss_justification: Relies on FLOSS implementations: Node.js with OpenSSL, Git, OpenSSH and GnuPG.
crypto_keylength_justification: The software generates no keys. The webhook secret is the HMAC-SHA256 key chosen by the operator; the configuration rejects secrets shorter than 32 characters, and the README tells operators to generate one with openssl rand -hex 32 (256 bits). Signing keys are the operator's SSH or GPG keys, checked by Git.
crypto_working_justification: No broken algorithms are used: webhook signatures use HMAC-SHA256; TLS and SSH use the defaults of Node.js, Git and OpenSSH.
crypto_pfs_justification: The software implements no key agreement protocol itself. TLS and SSH come from Node.js and Git/OpenSSH, whose defaults use ephemeral (EC)DHE key exchange.
crypto_password_storage_justification: The software does not store passwords for authenticating users.
crypto_random_justification: The software generates no cryptographic keys or nonces. The only random value is the optional poll jitter (Math.random), which has no security role.
delivery_mitm_justification: Delivered over HTTPS from npm, GitHub and ghcr.io. From 4.0.0 on, npm versions carry signed SLSA provenance, and the GitHub release tarball and the container image carry signed build attestations.
delivery_unsigned_justification: No hashes are retrieved over HTTP; npm verifies package integrity and provenance signatures, and container images are pulled by content digest over HTTPS.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: No medium or higher vulnerability in Self-Updater has been publicly known for more than 60 days. The one known finding in the container image, GO-2026-5932 (golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp in the Compose build), has no fixed version and is not reachable: Compose does not link the package, which govulncheck checks in CI (docker/compose/osv-scanner.toml).
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: Critical vulnerabilities are fixed as fast as possible according to the security policy; there are none open.
static_analysis_justification: CodeQL (security-extended and security-and-quality queries) runs on every pull request, every push to main and weekly; ESLint with typescript-eslint strictTypeChecked and eslint-plugin-sonarjs runs on every pull request with zero warnings allowed.
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: CodeQL with the security-extended query suite.
static_analysis_fixed_justification: There are no open CodeQL alerts and ESLint reports no issues; findings are fixed before merge because both are required checks.
static_analysis_often_justification: Static analysis runs on every pull request and every push to main; CodeQL also weekly.
dynamic_analysis_justification: Property-based tests with fast-check (test/properties.test.ts) generate random inputs for SemVer ordering, configuration, .env and environment parsing, secret redaction and webhook signature checks on every test run, and the full test suite runs before every release.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: The property-based and integration tests assert every invariant; at run time the configuration and all external input are validated and errors are thrown as typed SelfUpdaterError values.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: All issues found by dynamic analysis were fixed; none are open.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: By default nothing depends on weak algorithms: the only algorithm the software uses itself is HMAC-SHA256. Commit and tag signature checks (off by default) are done by Git and cover Git object ids, whose hash algorithm (SHA-1 with collision detection or SHA-256) is a property of the deployed repository.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: GitHub Actions runs the tests on every push and pull request on Ubuntu, Windows and macOS with Node 22 and 24. https://github.com/VectoDE/Self-Updater/actions/workflows/ci.yml
discussion_justification: GitHub issues, pull requests and Discussions are public and searchable: https://github.com/VectoDE/Self-Updater/discussions
no_leaked_credentials_justification: No credentials in the repository: gitleaks runs in CI, GitHub secret scanning with push protection is on, and npm publishes through OIDC Trusted Publishing without tokens. The only stored secrets are two SSH keys in the protected GitHub environment "release".
english_justification: All documentation, code, issues and discussions are in English; reports in English are welcome.
hardening_justification: No runtime dependencies; Git and built-in restarts run without a shell; the webhook receiver is off by default, listens on 127.0.0.1 by default and refuses to start without a secret; the systemd example runs as an unprivileged user with systemd sandboxing, and the container image runs as the non-root node user. CI and release runners use step-security/harden-runner, actions and base images are pinned by SHA or digest, and tokens are least privilege.
crypto_used_network_justification: Outgoing connections support HTTPS (provider API, Git, notifications) and SSH (Git). Plain http:// or git:// is only used when the operator configures such a URL. The webhook receiver speaks plain HTTP, is off by default and listens on 127.0.0.1 by default; it is meant to sit behind a reverse proxy that terminates TLS, as the README describes, and every delivery is authenticated with HMAC-SHA256 or the GitLab token.
crypto_tls12_justification: TLS is provided by Node.js and Git (libcurl), which use TLS 1.2 or later by default; the software does not change the TLS versions.
crypto_certificate_verification_justific: Node.js and Git verify TLS certificates by default, and the software never turns verification off (no rejectUnauthorized, NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED or http.sslVerify settings anywhere in the code).
crypto_verification_private_justificatio: The access token is only sent over connections whose certificate Node.js or Git has verified during the TLS handshake, before any HTTP header is sent. Git gets it as an http.<origin>.extraHeader scoped to the repository origin, so it goes nowhere else.
installation_common_justification: npm install --global @vectode/self-updater, or the container image ghcr.io/vectode/self-updater for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64. https://github.com/VectoDE/Self-Updater/blob/main/README.md#install
dco_justification: Commits must be signed off under the Developer Certificate of Origin; a workflow checks every commit of a pull request (bot commits are exempt). https://github.com/VectoDE/Self-Updater/blob/main/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md#commits-and-pull-requests
access_continuity_justification: The project has one maintainer. Code, history and releases are public and npm publishing needs no personal token (Trusted Publishing), but no second person can yet take over the repository, the npm packages and the @vectode scope. Tracked in https://github.com/VectoDE/Self-Updater/issues/13
bus_factor_justification: Single maintainer today. Continuity measures (public history, token-free OIDC publishing, documented release workflow) are in https://github.com/VectoDE/Self-Updater/blob/main/.github/GOVERNANCE.md#continuity
documentation_security_justification: What users can expect from security and how to verify releases: https://github.com/VectoDE/Self-Updater/blob/main/.github/SECURITY.md and https://github.com/VectoDE/Self-Updater/blob/main/docs/ASSURANCE.md
documentation_quick_start_justification: Install and first deployment in the README: https://github.com/VectoDE/Self-Updater/blob/main/README.md#quick-start
documentation_current_justification: Docs are updated in the same pull request as the code; the pull request template asks for README and changelog entries for new options. The README was rewritten for 4.0.0.
documentation_achievements_justification: The README shows the CI, OpenSSF Scorecard, npm and license badges; the Best Practices badge is added once this entry exists. https://github.com/VectoDE/Self-Updater/blob/main/README.md
accessibility_best_practices_justificati: The configuration builder (the only UI) uses semantic HTML with labelled controls, visible focus styles, a polite live region for validation results, a light and dark theme and respects reduced motion. https://github.com/VectoDE/Self-Updater/tree/main/site
internationalization_justification: CLI messages, logs and the configuration builder are in English only. Machine-readable output (--json, exit codes, error codes) lets other tools present results in other languages.
sites_password_security_justification: The project sites (GitHub, GitHub Pages, npm) do not store passwords of the project.
maintenance_or_update_justification: Supported versions are in the security policy: https://github.com/VectoDE/Self-Updater/blob/main/.github/SECURITY.md#supported-versions . Upgrading from self-updater 1.x-3.x is described in the README, and self-updater migrate converts old configuration files: https://github.com/VectoDE/Self-Updater/blob/main/README.md#upgrading-from-self-updater-1x-to-3x
vulnerability_report_credit_justificatio: Reporters are credited in the advisory and the changelog: https://github.com/VectoDE/Self-Updater/blob/main/.github/SECURITY.md#what-happens-next
coding_standards_enforced_justification: CI enforces TypeScript strict mode, typescript-eslint strictTypeChecked and stylisticTypeChecked, sonarjs and Prettier with zero warnings allowed.
build_preserve_debug_justification: The library build emits source maps next to the bundles, and the CLI bundle is not minified, so debugging information is kept.
build_non_recursive_justification: No make-style build; npm scripts call tsdown directly.
build_repeatable_justification: Builds use the committed package-lock.json with npm ci, exact development dependency versions and the Node version from .nvmrc; the container build pins base images by digest and the Compose modules through go.sum. Release builds run in GitHub Actions from the release commit.
installation_standard_variables_justific: Installed through npm or as a container image; no install script or file layout of its own.
installation_development_quick_justifica: git clone, npm ci, npm test. https://github.com/VectoDE/Self-Updater/blob/main/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md#setup
external_dependencies_justification: Development dependencies are listed in package.json with exact versions and locked with integrity hashes in package-lock.json; there are no runtime dependencies. The container image pins its base images by digest and builds Docker Compose from docker/compose/go.mod and go.sum.
dependency_monitoring_justification: Dependabot version and security updates cover npm, GitHub Actions, the Docker base images and the Go module of the Compose build. OSV-Scanner checks package-lock.json and docker/compose/go.mod daily and on every pull request, CI scans the built container image with OSV-Scanner and govulncheck, and npm audit and GitHub dependency review run on every pull request.
updateable_reused_components_justificati: Reused components are npm packages, Docker base images and Go modules, all updated through Dependabot and the lockfiles.
interfaces_current_justification: Uses current Node.js 22+ APIs (node:crypto, node:http, fetch) and current Git commands; no deprecated interfaces.
automated_integration_testing_justificat: CI builds the package, runs the built CLI (init, validate, update --dry-run), installs the packed tarball in a fresh project, loads the configuration entry on Deno and Bun, and builds the container image and checks that it runs as a non-root user with git and docker compose. https://github.com/VectoDE/Self-Updater/actions/workflows/ci.yml
regression_tests_added50_justification: The bug fixes of the last six months came with tests: the log redaction fix (99d486c) added regression tests, and the fixes to the container build are checked by the "Container image" CI job, which builds the image and runs git and docker compose in it.
test_statement_coverage80_justification: About 98 % statement coverage, enforced by thresholds in vitest.config.ts.
test_policy_mandated_justification: The contributing guide requires tests for new behaviour and a test that fails without the fix for every bug fix, and the pull request template asks for it. https://github.com/VectoDE/Self-Updater/blob/main/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md#making-a-change
implement_secure_design_justification: Secure design principles are applied as described in https://github.com/VectoDE/Self-Updater/blob/main/docs/ASSURANCE.md#secure-design-principles
input_validation_justification: The configuration is validated completely before anything runs (src/config/schema.ts), with strict patterns for branch, remote and service names and URL checks. Webhook deliveries are limited to 1 MB and authenticated before parsing, provider API answers are accepted only if they are a commit id, and refs reach Git only after -- or as full refspecs.
crypto_algorithm_agility_justification: The software implements no algorithms. The webhook algorithm is fixed by GitHub's protocol (X-Hub-Signature-256) and lives in one function in src/webhook.ts; signature algorithms are those of Git, OpenSSH and GnuPG and follow their configuration.
crypto_credential_agility_justification: The access token, webhook secret and notification URLs are referenced in the configuration as ${NAME} and read from the environment or a separate .env file, so they are kept apart from the configuration and can be changed without rebuilding. They never reach logs, .git/config or the state file.
signed_releases_justification: From 4.0.0 on, the release workflow publishes npm versions with signed SLSA provenance (Trusted Publishing), GitHub releases with the tarball, its signed build attestation (.intoto.jsonl) and a CycloneDX SBOM, and the container image ghcr.io/vectode/self-updater with a signed build attestation. Verification is documented in https://github.com/VectoDE/Self-Updater/blob/main/.github/SECURITY.md#verifying-a-release . The old package self-updater (3.0.0 and older) was published by hand without provenance.
version_tags_signed_justification: From v4.0.0 on, the release workflow signs every release commit and version tag with an SSH key kept only in the GitHub environment "release", which only main can use; the workflow verifies the tag before pushing it, and GitHub shows it as verified. Public key in .github/allowed_signers; verification in https://github.com/VectoDE/Self-Updater/blob/main/.github/SECURITY.md#verifying-a-release . The older tags v1.0.0, v1.0.1 and 1.0.2 are unsigned historical tags.
assurance_case_justification: Threat model, trust boundaries, secure design principles and countered weaknesses: https://github.com/VectoDE/Self-Updater/blob/main/docs/ASSURANCE.md
maintained_justification: Actively maintained: the 4.0.0 rewrite, weekly Dependabot updates, a public roadmap and open planning issues. https://github.com/VectoDE/Self-Updater/issues
OSPS-AC-02.01_justification: Collaborators can only be added by the owner through an explicit invitation; nobody gets access by default. Today the maintainer is the only collaborator.
OSPS-AC-03.01_justification: The ruleset "Protect main" blocks direct pushes: every change needs a pull request with 15 required status checks. Only the release workflow's deploy key may bypass it to push the release commit.
OSPS-AC-03.02_justification: The ruleset "Protect main" forbids deleting the main branch and force pushes; only the release deploy key can bypass it, and it only pushes release commits.
OSPS-BR-01.01_justification: Workflows pass untrusted metadata (pull request numbers and URLs, workflow inputs) only through environment variables, never inline in scripts; dispatch inputs are a fixed choice or validated against a strict pattern.
OSPS-BR-03.02_justification: Distribution channels (npm, GitHub releases, GitHub Packages, ghcr.io) use HTTPS exclusively.
OSPS-BR-07.01_justification: No credentials in the repository: gitleaks runs in CI, GitHub secret scanning with push protection is on, and npm publishes through OIDC Trusted Publishing without tokens. The only stored secrets are two SSH keys in the protected GitHub environment "release". [no_leaked_credentials]
OSPS-DO-01.01_justification: The README documents installation, quick start, every configuration option, the CLI commands, webhooks, notifications, running it with systemd, PM2 or Docker Compose, the container image and the migration from self-updater 1.x-3.x. The configuration builder at https://self-updater.pages.dev/ checks a configuration with the same validation code. https://github.com/VectoDE/Self-Updater/blob/main/README.md [documentation_basics]
OSPS-DO-02.01_justification: Bug reports go to GitHub issues with issue forms: https://github.com/VectoDE/Self-Updater/issues [report_process]
OSPS-GV-02.01_justification: GitHub supports public discussions on proposed changes (via pull requests) and usage obstacles (via issues and Discussions).
OSPS-GV-03.01_justification: Contributions go through GitHub pull requests; the process is documented in https://github.com/VectoDE/Self-Updater/blob/main/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md [contribution]
OSPS-LE-02.01_justification: The Apache-2.0 license for the repository contents is approved by the Open Source Initiative (OSI).
OSPS-LE-02.02_justification: Apache-2.0; the LICENSE file is included in the npm package and the container image is labelled with it. https://github.com/VectoDE/Self-Updater/blob/main/LICENSE [floss_license]
OSPS-QA-01.01_justification: Repository is publicly available on GitHub.
OSPS-QA-01.02_justification: Repository git metadata is publicly available on GitHub.
OSPS-QA-02.01_justification: Development dependencies are listed in package.json with exact versions and locked with integrity hashes in package-lock.json; there are no runtime dependencies. The container image pins its base images by digest and builds Docker Compose from docker/compose/go.mod and go.sum. [external_dependencies]
OSPS-QA-04.01_justification: The project consists of a single repository.
OSPS-QA-05.01_justification: No generated executables are committed; build output (dist/, site/dist/) and coverage are ignored by git and built in CI.
OSPS-QA-05.02_justification: The repository contains no binary artifacts.
OSPS-VM-02.01_justification: The reporting process is published in https://github.com/VectoDE/Self-Updater/blob/main/.github/SECURITY.md#reporting-a-vulnerability [vulnerability_report_process]
OSPS-AC-04.01_justification: The repository default for workflow tokens is read-only, and every workflow declares permissions: contents: read at the top; jobs only add what they need.
OSPS-BR-02.01_justification: Every release gets a unique SemVer version, from package.json and the git tag. https://github.com/VectoDE/Self-Updater/releases [version_unique]
OSPS-BR-04.01_justification: Human-readable release notes per version in https://github.com/VectoDE/Self-Updater/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md and on the GitHub releases (the release workflow uses the changelog section as the tag message and release notes). [release_notes]
OSPS-BR-05.01_justification: Development dependencies are listed in package.json with exact versions and locked with integrity hashes in package-lock.json; there are no runtime dependencies. Verification is documented in https://github.com/VectoDE/Self-Updater/blob/main/.github/SECURITY.md#verifying-a-release . The old package self-updater (3.0.0 and older) was published by hand without provenance. [signed_releases]
OSPS-DO-06.01_justification: How dependencies are selected, pinned and tracked: https://github.com/VectoDE/Self-Updater/blob/main/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md#dependencies
OSPS-GV-01.01_justification: Members with access to sensitive resources are listed in https://github.com/VectoDE/Self-Updater/blob/main/.github/GOVERNANCE.md#access-to-sensitive-resources
OSPS-LE-01.01_justification: Commits must be signed off under the Developer Certificate of Origin; a workflow checks every commit of a pull request (bot commits are exempt). https://github.com/VectoDE/Self-Updater/blob/main/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md#commits-and-pull-requests [dco]
OSPS-QA-03.01_justification: The ruleset "Protect main" requires 15 status checks (lint and types, tests on three operating systems and two Node versions, build and package checks, Deno and Bun, container image, configuration builder, dependency audit, CodeQL, DCO sign-off) to pass before a pull request can be merged.

OSPS-VM-04.01_justification: No release so far fixed a publicly known vulnerability. The security policy requires fixed vulnerabilities to be listed under "Security" in the changelog, with the CVE where one applies. https://github.com/VectoDE/Self-Updater/blob/main/.github/SECURITY.md#what-happens-next [release_notes_vulns]
OSPS-AC-04.02_justification: Every workflow sets contents: read at the top; jobs only add the permissions their steps need (e.g. id-token and attestations for provenance, packages for GitHub Packages and ghcr.io, contents: write only for creating the GitHub release).
OSPS-BR-02.02_justification: Every released asset carries the release version: the npm tarball, the GitHub release assets (tarball, attestation, SBOM) and the container image tag.
OSPS-BR-07.02_justification: Policy for storing, accessing and rotating secrets: https://github.com/VectoDE/Self-Updater/blob/main/.github/SECURITY.md#secrets-and-credentials
OSPS-DO-03.01_justification: From 4.0.0 on, the release workflow publishes npm versions with signed SLSA provenance (Trusted Publishing), GitHub releases with the tarball, its signed build attestation (.intoto.jsonl) and a CycloneDX SBOM, and the container image ghcr.io/vectode/self-updater with a signed build attestation. Verification is documented in https://github.com/VectoDE/Self-Updater/blob/main/.github/SECURITY.md#verifying-a-release . The old package self-updater (3.0.0 and older) was published by hand without provenance. [signed_releases]
OSPS-DO-03.02_justification: From 4.0.0 on, the release workflow publishes npm versions with signed SLSA provenance (Trusted Publishing), GitHub releases with the tarball, its signed build attestation (.intoto.jsonl) and a CycloneDX SBOM, and the container image ghcr.io/vectode/self-updater with a signed build attestation. Verification is documented in https://github.com/VectoDE/Self-Updater/blob/main/.github/SECURITY.md#verifying-a-release . The old package self-updater (3.0.0 and older) was published by hand without provenance. [signed_releases]
OSPS-DO-04.01_justification: Scope and duration of support per release line: https://github.com/VectoDE/Self-Updater/blob/main/.github/SECURITY.md#supported-versions
OSPS-DO-05.01_justification: When versions stop getting security updates: https://github.com/VectoDE/Self-Updater/blob/main/.github/SECURITY.md#supported-versions
OSPS-GV-04.01_justification: Collaborators are reviewed before getting escalated permissions: https://github.com/VectoDE/Self-Updater/blob/main/.github/GOVERNANCE.md#access-to-sensitive-resources
OSPS-QA-02.02_justification: Every GitHub release carries a CycloneDX SBOM next to the signed tarball; the package has no runtime dependencies. The container image is pushed with a BuildKit SBOM attestation. https://github.com/VectoDE/Self-Updater/blob/main/.github/SECURITY.md#verifying-a-release
OSPS-QA-04.02_justification: The project consists of a single repository.
OSPS-QA-06.02_justification: Automated test suite with Vitest: unit tests, integration tests that deploy, roll back, follow tags and check SSH signatures against real Git repositories created in the temp directory, and property-based tests with fast-check. Run with npm test, documented in https://github.com/VectoDE/Self-Updater/blob/main/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md#setup . Tests: https://github.com/VectoDE/Self-Updater/tree/main/test [test]
OSPS-QA-06.03_justification: The contributing guide requires tests for new behaviour and a test that fails without the fix for every bug fix, and the pull request template asks for it. https://github.com/VectoDE/Self-Updater/blob/main/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md#making-a-change [test_policy_mandated]
OSPS-QA-07.01_justification: The project has a single maintainer, so no second person can approve changes yet. Every change still goes through a pull request with 15 required checks (tests, CodeQL, dependency audit, DCO). Required approvals will be switched on once a second maintainer joins, as described in https://github.com/VectoDE/Self-Updater/blob/main/.github/GOVERNANCE.md#decisions
OSPS-SA-03.02_justification: Threat model, trust boundaries, secure design principles and countered weaknesses: https://github.com/VectoDE/Self-Updater/blob/main/docs/ASSURANCE.md [assurance_case]
OSPS-VM-04.02_justification: The package has no runtime dependencies. Findings in the container image that do not apply and have no fix are published as OpenVEX statements: https://github.com/VectoDE/Self-Updater/blob/main/.vex/self-updater.openvex.json (currently GO-2026-5932, not linked; govulncheck checks the binaries in CI). Policy: https://github.com/VectoDE/Self-Updater/blob/main/.github/SECURITY.md#vulnerabilities-in-dependencies
OSPS-VM-05.01_justification: Dependabot version and security updates cover npm, GitHub Actions, the Docker base images and the Go module of the Compose build. OSV-Scanner checks package-lock.json and docker/compose/go.mod daily and on every pull request, CI scans the built container image with OSV-Scanner and govulncheck, and npm audit and GitHub dependency review run on every pull request. [dependency_monitoring]
OSPS-VM-05.02_justification: Dependency vulnerabilities are fixed by updating before release; the policy is in https://github.com/VectoDE/Self-Updater/blob/main/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md#dependencies and https://github.com/VectoDE/Self-Updater/blob/main/.github/SECURITY.md#vulnerabilities-in-dependencies . Dependabot version and security updates cover npm, GitHub Actions, the Docker base images and the Go module of the Compose build. OSV-Scanner checks package-lock.json and docker/compose/go.mod daily and on every pull request, CI scans the built container image with OSV-Scanner and govulncheck, and npm audit and GitHub dependency review run on every pull request.
OSPS-VM-05.03_justification: Required status checks before merge include npm audit --audit-level=moderate and the container image scan (OSV-Scanner and govulncheck). GitHub dependency review also runs on every pull request and fails on moderate or higher vulnerabilities and on denied licenses.
OSPS-VM-06.01_justification: There are no open CodeQL alerts and ESLint reports no issues; findings are fixed before merge because both are required checks. [static_analysis_fixed]
OSPS-VM-06.02_justification: CodeQL (security-extended and security-and-quality queries) runs on every pull request, every push to main and weekly; ESLint with typescript-eslint strictTypeChecked and eslint-plugin-sonarjs runs on every pull request with zero warnings allowed. [static_analysis]
OSPS-BR-01.03_justification: Pull request workflows run on pull_request (not pull_request_target) with read-only tokens and no secrets. Secrets and publishing rights exist only in workflows on main; the release keys are in the environment "release", used by one job that runs no dependency code.
OSPS-DO-07.01_justification: git clone, npm ci, npm test. https://github.com/VectoDE/Self-Updater/blob/main/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md#setup [installation_development_quick]
OSPS-BR-01.04_justification: Manual workflow inputs are validated before use: the version step is a fixed choice, a tag must match a strict version pattern, exist and point to a commit on main; all inputs reach scripts only through environment variables.
copyright_per_file_justification: Every source file starts with an SPDX-FileCopyrightText header naming the copyright holder (Vecto). Files that cannot carry a comment (Markdown, JSON, tool settings) are covered by REUSE.toml. CI runs the REUSE check on every pull request: https://github.com/VectoDE/Self-Updater/blob/main/REUSE.toml
license_per_file_justification: Every source file has an SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0 header; the rest is covered by REUSE.toml, and the license text is in LICENSES/. CI fails when a file has no license information: https://github.com/VectoDE/Self-Updater/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml
code_review_standards_justification: The contributing guide lists what every review checks (purpose, correctness, tests, security, dependencies, compatibility, documentation, style) and when a reviewer approves: https://github.com/VectoDE/Self-Updater/blob/main/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md#code-review
build_reproducible_justification: CI builds the npm package from two separate clones in different directories and fails unless both tarballs have the same SHA-256 (job "Reproducible package"): https://github.com/VectoDE/Self-Updater/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml
hardened_site_justification: The project site (https://self-updater.pages.dev/) is served by Cloudflare Pages with Content-Security-Policy, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy from site/_headers. github.com and npmjs.com send HSTS, CSP, X-Content-Type-Options and X-Frame-Options. The old GitHub Pages address only forwards to the new site.
